READ THIS FIRST
There is no honest single 'usage %' for every programming language. This workbook keeps separate metrics: GitHub public-code activity, Stack Overflow self-reported usage, and TIOBE search/popularity rating. Country data and gender data have different coverage and should not be inferred where absent.
Notable current/historical executable languages and DSLs, under 1,000 entries.
GitHub supports language-by-economy counts; this pack includes methodology plus a verified Bangladesh example and SO respondent geography.
Per-language male/female percentages are intentionally not fabricated. JetBrains 2025 raw survey is a suitable source for future cross-tabs.
Gender data notes: Can we publish male/female % for every language?
JetBrains 2025 includes gender and language variables and offers anonymized raw survey data.
No reliable published per-language male/female percentages were verified in this research pass.
Do not invent values. Cross-tab the raw survey, publish sample sizes, include non-binary/prefer-not-to-say categories, and label it as survey data.
Can we call survey gender shares 'all programmers'?
No. Surveys describe their respondents, subject to sampling/weighting choices.
They are not a census of the global developer population.
Use wording such as 'among respondents to the 2025 JetBrains Developer Ecosystem Survey'.
Should CODARIS force binary gender categories?
The cited JetBrains report includes Male, Female, Prefer not to say, and Non-binary/genderqueer/gender non-conforming.
A binary-only table would discard reported categories.
Preserve the source categories and allow 'unknown / not reported' rather than guessing.
Methodology: Topic
Rule used in this pack
Why it matters
Catalogue scope
Uses the English Wikipedia index of notable programming languages. It is not a claim to contain every language ever created.
Thousands of experimental, esoteric, dialect and internal languages exist; a bounded educational catalogue needs a declared scope.
HTML/CSS

Included in Stack Overflow usage rankings because that survey category explicitly includes programming, scripting and markup languages, but not added to the core programming-language catalogue because the catalogue source excludes markup languages.
Prevents mixing incompatible taxonomies.
GitHub metric
Unique developers in an economy making at least one git push to a repository containing a language during a quarter.
Measures public GitHub coding activity, not total programmers, jobs, lines of code, or private work.
GitHub geography
Economy based on GitHub methodology; data is quarterly and public-only; low-count economies may be withheld.
Country comparisons can be incomplete and should not be treated as census estimates.
Stack Overflow usage
Self-reported extensive development work in the past year; multiple languages can be selected.
Percentages overlap and do not add to 100.
Stack Overflow countries
Where survey respondents live.
Useful for sample composition only, not for ranking the total developer population by country.
TIOBE
Popularity index derived from search/activity signals around skilled engineers, courses, vendors and web sources.
It is not a direct measure of actual language usage.
Gender
No per-language percentages are populated unless a source directly supports them.
Avoids false precision and demographic fabrication.
Ranking
No composite 'best language' score is created.
Different sources measure different constructs; combining them without a defensible model would be misleading.
